title: Distributional Shift Robustness of Reward Models: Evaluation on Out-of-Distribution Prompt Types

original_idea.problem: Reward model reliability on out-of-distribution prompt types is poorly understood.
original_idea.direction: Train a small reward model on HH-RLHF chat preference data. Evaluate on three held-out domains: code generation, math reasoning, creative writing. Measure rank correlation between reward model scores and human preferences.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: characterizing reward model OOD degradation informs which domains need domain-specific reward models. The safety relevance is real but somewhat indirect — the link from OOD reward model failures to specific safety failures requires an additional step (how PPO exploits these failures).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training a reward model, sourcing or creating evaluation data across three domains, and implementing rank correlation evaluation. Reward model training and preference data handling are non-trivial for beginners. The multi-domain evaluation setup adds significant overhead.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple workstreams: train reward model, prepare 3 domain evaluation sets, evaluate and compute correlations. The deliverable exists but depends on resolving several unknowns (evaluation data quality, proxy human evaluation via GPT-4). May stretch 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: 'On the Robustness of Reward Models for Language Model Alignment' (ICML 2025) directly evaluates reward model robustness under distribution shift. 'Robust Reward Model Training Mitigating...' (ICLR 2025) proposes solutions. 'An Empirical Study on Preference Tuning Generalization and Diversity Under Domain Shift' (arXiv:2601.05882, 2026) systematically characterizes preference model degradation across domains. The specific experiment — training on HH-RLHF and evaluating on code/math/creative writing — is a standard cross-domain evaluation that is substantially covered by existing literature on reward model OOD robustness.
